findings.issue: The via-IR optimizer folded keccak256(204), the data base of the `_name` string, into a constant, which the text prints as a bare 64-digit number (next to a dead `mem[0] = 204`) instead of `sha3(204)` / `name[...]`; the return copy is a word-by-word while (P7) and the allocation size `floor32(_3 - 97)` is opaque.
findings.rule: Recognise constants equal to keccak256(n) for small slot numbers n (a precomputed table) and print them as `sha3(n)`, which also lets the storage analysis name the array; print a memory-to-memory word copy as a copy line.

notes: All functions are short (under 100 lines); all reviewed. Source loop: StringsUpgradeable.toHexString (`while idx > 1`), inlined twice per onlyRole function (mint, burn, grantRole, revokeRole, transferAllRoles) for the AccessControl revert message, as in c00506. Implicit: name/symbol return copies and the upgradeToAndCall bytes copy (P7). P11: the bounds checks `if idx >= 42/66: revert Panic(50)` inside `while idx > 1` loops starting at 41/65, and `require calldata.size - 4 >=′ 0` behind the dispatcher. No semantic error found.
summary: Clean, faithful text; the only source loop (toHexString) is a clear while, with minor issues: a folded keccak slot constant printed as a raw number and redundant bounds checks.
